title: PROSE: Graph Structure Learning via Progressive Strategy

problem.claim: Graph neural network node representations depend strongly on graph structure, while real-world graph topologies inevitably contain noise such as irrelevant or missing edges.

gap.claim: Existing graph structure learning methods are described as status-unaware because they judge all node connections simultaneously with one monotonous standard, causing indeterminacy and instability during optimization.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes PROSE, a graph structure learning model that uses a progressive, status-aware strategy to acquire graph structure.
PROSE includes progressive structure splitting and progressive structure refining modules that modify node connections according to global potency.
PROSE introduces horizontal and vertical position encodings to capture graph topology information described as ignored by previous methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present PROSE as a new model for graph structure learning via a progressive strategy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Exploratory experiments on publicly available datasets produced observations that motivated the proposed model.
Experiments on several widely used graph datasets are reported to demonstrate the effectiveness of PROSE.
The authors provide a source-code link for PROSE.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNN representation quality depends on graph structure, which can be noisy in real-world settings.
Graph structure learning addresses noisy connections, but existing methods are characterized as status-unaware and unstable.
Exploratory experiments on public datasets yielded observations supporting the authors' perspective.
The authors propose PROSE, using progressive structure splitting, refining, and positional encodings for status-aware graph structure learning.
Experiments on several widely used graph datasets are reported, with source code provided.

source_observation.claim: The abstract identifies a limitation in applying one uniform connection-judgment standard to nodes with different statuses.

interpretation.claim: Learning procedures may benefit from adapting structural decisions to heterogeneous node conditions.

application.claim: When designing graph structure learning methods, consider progressive and status-aware connection modification.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported graph datasets or settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the progressive modules or positional encodings.
The abstract does not specify the meaning or operationalization of node status and global potency.
